meta.title: The Gate That Sends Boxes Two Ways
meta.skill_frame: Process: see where one test sends the work two ways.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: Measured FK 6.18, 5.37 and 5.26 on the three parts (105, 111 and 107 words), 5.58 together, near the band's floor. The load is one test early in the chain that decides between two routes. Later steps never read the label again, so the reader has to see that a wrong branch cannot be repaired downstream.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for process 4.1, band 4.1, sequence 1. No external work.
source.text_status: Drafted for the band, accepted on spot check.
source.survey: A parcel hub where one scan sends boxes to a town chute or an airport container; the test sits upstream of a sealed step, so a wrong branch cannot be repaired later.
source.avoided: No company, city, code format, or volume figure. No claim about how many boxes a container holds.

session.difficulty_basis: One test at one step sends the work two ways; later steps never re-check, so the reader must connect the branch to the sealed container.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: A trailer backs up to the first gate, and the boxes ride a belt toward a scanner. The scanner reads the label on each box. It compares the code with the route list for the day. A box carrying the local code turns onto the near belt, and every other box continues onto the far belt. The gate does not open a box or weigh it, and it only reads the label and sends the box one of two ways. A torn label stops the belt until a worker reads the printed code by hand and types it in, because the list changes at midnight.
passage.part_2: The two belts lead to different work. The near belt drops boxes down a short chute, where a worker stacks them by street for the town vans. The far belt carries boxes into a steel container that is sealed and driven to the airport. A local box that rides the far belt will be flown far away and come back days later. The gate checks the code once, and nothing on the far route reads the label again. The near chute is cleared twice an hour, because a full chute backs boxes up onto the belt. A full container leaves on the hour, whether or not the belt is still running.
passage.part_3: The order is set by the sealed container. Once the doors close, no worker can open it to look for a stray box, so the test has to happen while the box is still on the open belt. The same rule holds when a label fails. The belt stops, the code is read by hand, and the box is sent on one of the same two routes. The branch is decided at the gate, and every later step trusts that decision. A wrong send is not repaired later, because the box is already on its way to another town. Nothing is sent back once the doors close.

items.prompt: What does the scanner read on each box?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The label on the box.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The second sentence says the scanner reads the label on each box.
tutor_only.tell: The scanner reads the label. The code on it decides which belt the box takes.
help: The second sentence says what the scanner reads.
It is printed on the outside of the box.
tutor_only.core_idea: The label on the box, with its code.
accept_ideas: the printed code on the box
